_note: Quiz bank for Jeffrey's YouTube Bootcamp. 'answer' is a 0-based index into options.

questions.q: What is a YouTuber's actual job, in one line?
options: Make videos people choose to watch again and again
questions.why: Everything else — money, fans, sponsors — is a result of that one sentence.

questions.q: What does the algorithm reward FIRST?
questions.why: Reliability first. One video a week for months beats ten videos then silence.

questions.q: Most channels die at which video?
questions.why: Most people quit around video three. Not quitting is the whole trick.

questions.q: Which niche is stronger for starting?
questions.why: Narrow beats broad. A few hundred competitors, not 50 million.

questions.q: Why write 10 video ideas BEFORE video 1?
options: Channels die when video 2 has no idea
questions.why: The 'what do I make next?' gap is what kills most channels.

questions.q: What is the 'One Viewer' trick?
options: Make videos for one specific person with one problem
questions.why: Videos made 'for everyone' are watched by no one.

questions.q: Which channel name is best?
questions.why: Easy to say and spell, works everywhere, not locked to one game.

questions.q: Why is 'my gameplay #4' a bad video idea?
options: It has no clear promise — nobody clicks it
questions.why: Every video needs a clear promise in the title, not a number.

questions.q: What must the first 8-15 seconds do?
options: Deliver the hook — who it's for and what they get
questions.why: Viewers decide in ~8 seconds. 'Hey guys welcome back' loses them.

questions.q: What is retention?
options: The % of the video people actually watch
questions.why: Retention is the biggest ranking signal. Keep people watching.

questions.q: You're 12 and don't want to show your face. Best option?
questions.why: Voice + gameplay is perfect for gaming — connection without exposure.

questions.q: What matters more than a fancy camera?
questions.why: Clear audio and tight editing. The camera barely matters.

questions.q: What decides your CTR?
questions.why: CTR is decided before anyone watches — it's the packaging.

questions.q: What's a good target CTR?
questions.why: 4–10% is solid. Below that, fix the thumbnail and title.

questions.q: Why make the thumbnail BEFORE editing?
options: If you can't make a compelling thumbnail, the video isn't compelling
questions.why: The thumbnail is the promise. If it doesn't work, rethink the video.

questions.q: What's the smart play with Shorts?
options: Cut the best 30 seconds of your long video as a Short pointing to it
Make Shorts instead of long videos
questions.why: One effort, two products. Shorts for discovery, long videos for the audience.

questions.q: When should you judge your channel's success?
questions.why: The 20-video deal: first 10 are practice, 10–20 is where style emerges.

questions.q: What does the YouTube Partner Program require?
options: 1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours (or 10M Shorts views), and 13+
questions.why: And realistically it's 6–18 months of consistent work away.

questions.q: Which is NEVER okay to share?
options: Your school, address or daily routine
questions.why: Viewers include people you don't want knowing your location or routine.

questions.q: Why should you not read out hate comments on camera?
options: It feeds the trolls and hurts you
questions.why: Trolls want the reaction. Block, delete, move on.
